prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B001 prize to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange was unanimous on the trio, so I tested it against the chair's questions instead of leaning on agreement. The merit case stands on the mechanism-to-therapy arc: gut-hormone physiology and the insulinotropic and glucagonostatic actions (Holst), the biology and receptor-mediated actions across tissues (Drucker), and identification and synthesis of the bioactive GLP-1(7-36) amide (Mojsov). That work was independently confirmed over decades and then validated in large randomized trials for glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. Maturity is not in doubt. The physiology-led citation also names a discovery that is complete and specific, rather than a drug class, and I would keep the citation wording that says the discoveries made possible the therapy so that it does not read as a prize for one product.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness, and round 1 did not remove it. Knudsen's acylation chemistry produced the long-acting analogues that reached patients, so a physiology trio can be read as honouring the hormone and not the drugs. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide relative to Habener's group is contested, and none of us has cited a document that settles it. Several of us, including me, are relying on general knowledge. If the committee judged that Mojsov's role could not be defended, the prize would stall on credit, not on science, and that would be a substantive change of configuration. I would not make that change on the present record, but I want the uncertainty stated plainly and not smoothed over by the unanimous tally.

responses.point: The chair's question asks whether B001 should be physiology-led or drug-development-led, and which discovery-side laureate would be omitted if Knudsen were included. His own file also leaves open whether a single-achievement prize is stronger than a two-part prize, and it flags Habener as an awkward absence.
responses.response: I would answer the first question by principle, not by head count. The citation should honour the discovery that made the drugs possible, and the cap then forces the physiology trio. If Knudsen were added, I see no principled way to drop one of the three. Holst established the physiology, Drucker the biology and receptor actions, and Mojsov the active peptide, and removing any of them breaks the arc the prize is meant to honour. Dropping Mojsov in particular would let a contested priority question decide the outcome without our having resolved it. On the second question I keep a single part. A second achievement would take slots from a trio that already leaves out Knudsen and Habener, and it would weaken both parts. On Habener, I agree the absence is awkward, but the priority question is not documented in our files, so I will not rewrite the credited names on recollection.

responses.point: Sandberg treats Knudsen's work as drug design and not discovery, and he calls Mojsov's contribution decisive yet contested. His own alternatives are B051 (unfolded protein response) and B017, and he asks how much clinical translation should count for B051 and B050.
responses.response: I moved partly toward you since round 1. I still would not call Knudsen's work merely industrial, but I now think the stronger argument is about what the citation honours, not about whether her chemistry mattered. On Mojsov we agree that the question is open, and your remark that it is a reason to deliberate over names and not to demote the discovery is the position I hold. On translation versus mechanism, B001 is the one candidate that is complete on both sides, so it need not be tested against the weaker standard. I would not use the lack of clinical validation to dismiss B051 or B050, because a clean mechanistic discovery can be Nobel-scale. But for this year I rank them below B017 because B017 has a new therapeutic modality with outcome evidence, which makes it the more defensible fallback.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks the unfolded protein response (B051) third, ahead of CAR-T, as a conceptually clean two-person pair that is textbook after about three decades. His file also notes that Habener belongs in the GLP-1 priority discussion.
responses.response: On B051 I accept the textbook status and the clean Mori-Walter attribution, and I agree that maturity counts in its favour. My disagreement is about ordering. The PERK/eIF2 arm is not credited, as Sandberg noted, and disease-level consequences are still being worked out, so a B051 prize would rest on conceptual originality alone. I would hold it ahead of nothing on the shortlist this year, but I would not object to it appearing in a later cycle. On Habener I agree with your reasoning that he belongs in the discussion. Where I differ is on remedy. Because the supplied files cannot divide the priority, I would not change the credited names but would write the citation so that it describes the discovery of the active form without asserting an exclusive first.

responses.point: El-Manira names Holst, Drucker and Knudsen as the fallback if Mojsov's priority is judged too unclear, and he proposes Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel as one defensible trio for optogenetics (B012).
responses.response: I take the Holst-Drucker-Knudsen fallback seriously, because it shows what the committee would do if the priority question went against Mojsov, and I agree it would be a substantive change and not a detail. I would not trigger it on the present record, since nothing in the supplied materials shows her claim to be weaker than the others. On B012, your trio of Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel is defensible, and I thank you for stating a concrete principle. My concern remains that the omitted contributions (Bamberg's channel electrophysiology, Boyden's neuronal deployment, Miesenbock's earlier concept) are each necessary, so I would still keep B012 as an alternative and not as a preferred configuration. If B001 stalled, I would weigh B012 and B017 and lean toward B017, because it has the smaller credit gap and clinical evidence.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius places TNF blockade (B010) second as a clean, mature pair that is arguably overdue, and she asks whether Eshhar's early receptor work should alter the CAR-T credited set.
responses.response: On Eshhar I agree it is a live question, and I raised it in round 1. For B017 I would keep June, Sadelain and Rosenberg only if the citation is written around engineered T cells as a therapy, and I accept that Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept would then be an acknowledged omission. I do not think that gap prevents a B017 prize, but it makes it harder to defend than B001. On B010, I agree with you that the two-person attribution is clean, and I see no scientific objection to it. I still rank it below B017 because TNF blockade confirmed a cytokine hypothesis through a therapy, while engineered T cells opened a new modality. I would call that a judgment about novelty, not a disagreement about maturity, and your point that age should not be ignored is fair. Age alone, however, should not carry B010 or B008 above a candidate that is as mature and has greater reach.

uncertainties: Whether the priority for identifying and synthesising the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide divides in a way that should change the named laureates. I have no document in our supplied files that settles it, and I am relying on general knowledge.
Whether a physiology-led citation will be read as honouring the hormone and not the therapy, and whether the wording made possible is enough to answer that.
If B001 stalls, whether B017 is more defensible than B012, given the omitted Eshhar for CAR-T and the cut from six names to three for optogenetics.
Whether excluding Habener and Knudsen is a defect of the cap or a defect of the configuration.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B001, B017 or B012, and my disclosure is unchanged from round 1. My spatial transcriptomics co-authorship and my past co-authors (for example Betsholtz, Frisen, Ernfors, Castelo-Branco, Sandberg) are not credited names on any shortlisted ballot, and I will not infer other ties from shared institutions or topics.
